content: WAL is a persistent database-file property: set once and all processes pick it up (sqlite.org pragma docs). WAL gives one writer plus concurrent readers; readers do not block the writer. busy_timeout is per-connection and must be set on every new connection to wait instead of failing instantly with SQLITE_BUSY; modernc defaults the busy timeout to 0 while mattn historically defaulted to 5000ms. Recommended multi-process pragma set: journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=5000, synchronous=NORMAL (safe with WAL, one less fsync per commit). SQLITE_BUSY can still occur when the timeout elapses or on a read-to-write upgrade of a deferred transaction; BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the writer lock at BEGIN so writers queue instead. WAL does not work over network filesystems; every process needs write access to the directory holding the -wal/-shm sidecars. The last connection close checkpoints and deletes the WAL; long-lived readers can cause checkpoint starvation. In-memory databases cannot use WAL: their journal mode remains memory/off and change attempts are ignored.
